Welcome! This course teaches R programming for the full data-analysis workflow:
wrangling, visualization, simulation, and reproducible reporting with
[Quarto](https://quarto.org), using public-health data throughout. You will
also learn two skills that now define professional statistical programming:
managing code with **Git and GitHub**, and using **AI coding assistants
responsibly** (prompting, verifying, and debugging AI-generated code).

No prior programming or statistics experience is required.

## How the course works

- **Hands-on classes.** Every session alternates short live-coding demos with
  paired exercises, so you write code in every class.
- **Instant feedback.** Weekly exercises are submitted on GitHub and checked
  automatically: push your work, see which questions pass, revise, and resubmit
  until the deadline.
- **AI, embraced and verified.** AI tools are allowed on homework and the
  project (with disclosure), taught explicitly in Week 8, and set aside during
  short in-class quizzes where your own fluency is certified.
- **One real project.** The course builds to an individual analysis of a
  public-health dataset: a reproducible Quarto report, a GitHub repo, and a
  5-minute video walkthrough.

## Getting started (before Week 1)

1. Install [R](https://cloud.r-project.org/), then
   [RStudio Desktop](https://docs.posit.co/ide/user/#rstudio-ide-oss-downloads) (both free).
2. Create a free [GitHub account](https://github.com/signup) with your NYU email.
3. That's it. We will set up everything else together in the first class.

Step-by-step instructions, including installing Git and connecting it to
RStudio, are in the [setup guides](guides/index.qmd). Those pages stay up all
semester, so use them as the reference whenever something breaks.
